 DeMar DeRozan delivers in big spot for Denver Nuggets
 By Vinny Benedetto 
 Published November 19, 2026 12:35pm 
 | 
 Updated November 19, 2026 1:39pm 
 + 
 Add Denver Gazette on Google
 Denver Nuggets guard DeMar DeRozan, right, shoots for a basket as Boston Celtics guard Derrick White defends in the second half of an NBA basketball game Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in Denver. (AP Photo/David Zalubowski) 
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
 After the Nuggets ’ win Wednesday, DeMar DeRozan has as many appearances off the bench this season as he did in the first 17 years of his NBA career combined.
 “I would be lying to tell you it ain’t tough,” DeRozan admitted after his 12 th time coming off the bench as a Nugget. “It’s tough.”

 It looked tough for most of DeRozan’s first dozen games in Denver. He was scoring less efficiently than he did when he was a rookie with the Raptors back in 2009-10, which accounted for the other 12 appearances as a reserve.
 “There’s still so much learning, trying to get comfortable with, get accustomed with doing something for the first time in 17 years,” DeRozan said. “I’m just trying to figure out how, when, how much I can dictate the game when I’m out there, what I see before I go in.”
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
 While it’s still a work in progress, DeRozan is making progress. Nuggets coach David Adelman liked what he saw from the 37-year-old on Denver’s four-game road trip, but that was followed by a challenging night against the Suns when DeRozan scored two points on six shots in 14 minutes. He earned 25 minutes Wednesday, scored 18 points on 11 shots and played all but a handful of seconds of the fourth quarter when Denver outscored Boston, 25-21, in a 105-101 victory.
 “Nothing’s perfect right now. We’re trying to figure it out — DeMar and the team,” Adelman said. “I thought tonight he caught a rhythm. He became our third scorer, which we need to win games.”
 Adelman changed up his rotation a bit to get DeRozan into the game a little earlier in the first quarter. It took a while to see results. DeRozan had two points at the end of the first quarter, five points at halftime and failed to score in a short stint late in the third quarter. Adelman rode his starters for the first 10 minutes of the third. That meant using a five-man bench unit to start the fourth quarter in a tie game.
 Denver Nuggets guard DeMar DeRozan, center, drives past Boston Celtics center Luka Garza, left, and guard Payton Pritchard try to defend in the second half of an NBA basketball game Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in Denver. (AP Photo/David Zalubowski) 
 The veteran missed his first two shots of the fourth, and Boston scored the first four points of the quarter. Then, DeRozan got to the line for the time of the night. DeRozan has developed a deft ability to draw fouls thanks to a series of fakes and slight bumps that either get defenders to leave their feet or concede space to shoot an uncontested jumper.
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
 “I think he baits a lot of players. His midrange is deadly,” Nikola Jokic said. “You always think you can block the shot, but you can’t. He’s a really good basketball player.”
 DeRozan was an All-Star as recently as 2023. The season before, he finished 10 th in Most Valuable Player voting and was a second-team All-NBA selection. He turned back the clock a bit in the fourth quarter of Denver’s biggest win of the season. The six-time All-Star followed up his first trip to the line with two more free throws and three midrange jumpers that kept Denver within two in the middle of the fourth. He stayed out there as Jokic and Jamal Murray returned to the court to close out the game.
 “I just tried to take advantage of those opportunities when those guys drew so much attention,” DeRozan said. “I tried to just be aggressive, tried to score, tried to get easy points, also tried to create when I could. They made it easy on me. I try to take advantage of that.”
 The final three points of DeRozan’s night came from the free throw line. He said that was a conscious effort against the Celtics. At the end of the night, Boston was called for 30 fouls to Denver’s 13. The Nuggets took 29 free throws to Boston’s 12, and DeRozan’s eight free throws led all players. He said it was a conscious effort on his end in an attempt to make the pace of his game more favorable for his new team.
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
 “He was fantastic tonight. It was very old-school DeMar DeRozan — kind of owning possessions, owning the pace. It was fun to watch,” Adelman said.
 “It’s just so many years of mastering that and understanding body control and body contact. That’s a very aggressive team, very handsy team and a good defensive team.”
 DeRozan’s performance was undeniably a step in the right direction, but it was also just the second time in his first 12 games as a Nugget he exceeded 15 points in his short Nuggets tenure. He’s doing something he hasn’t done in a long time, after all.
 “Every moment has been a learning curve for me,” DeRozan said. “I just want to continue to get better at it.”
